run.question:
Can you help me check recent logs? We had a DR test in prod starting 6 hours ago.
companyopswebjob seemed to have some issues while a user was performing a test to
create a new scheduled job. It failed with 500s.
Please search the app-254-prod-logs index for relevant logs.

report.summary: I searched app-254-prod-logs (open/green, docs.count 12) across the query window 2026-11-23T10:00:00Z–17:12:59Z and it returned exactly 12 documents, all within timestamp 11:12:49Z–16:12:49Z. No document in this index carries a service value of companyopswebjob: the only service values present are Company.Ops (7 documents) and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (5 documents). So the exact entity the user named has no data here, while the similarly named but distinct service Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob does log errors. The logs do corroborate the reported symptom on Company.Ops: a DR test (correlation_id dr-test-001) is recorded at 11:12:49Z as 'switching to failover database', roughly 6 hours before the window end, and during the failover Company.Ops logs 'Job scheduler failed to process batch: connection timeout to failover DB after 30s' and 'Scheduled job execution failed with status 500: unable to acquire database lock during failover' (12:12:49Z), 'Job creation endpoint returning 503 - database failover in progress' (13:12:49Z), and, for the new-job creation attempt (correlation_id job-8831, 14:12:49Z), 'Failed to create new scheduled job: HTTP 500 - transaction deadlock detected on jobs table'. Logs then record 'DR test failover completed - primary database restored' (15:12:49Z) and 'Job scheduler resumed normal operation' (16:12:49Z), with no ERROR-level document after 14:12:49Z in the returned set. Every error message itself attributes the failure to the failover, which makes the database failover the leading hypothesis, but the failover database is not a named object in any evidence here and no metric, trace or cluster object confirms the mechanism, so the conclusion is partial and no root-cause object is named. Trace and metric sources could not be reached in this Run (Jaeger and Prometheus label queries both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), and the Kubernetes cluster I can read is the otel-demo cluster, which has no workload matching ops/radar/webjob.

claims.text: The index app-254-prod-logs exists, is open with health green, and reports docs.count 12 and store.size 10.1kb at query time.

A sorted search of app-254-prod-logs over 2026-11-23T10:00:00Z–17:12:59Z on the index's date field 'timestamp' returned 12 documents (total 12), spanning writer timestamps 2026-11-23T11:12:49Z to 2026-11-23T16:12:49Z.

The only values of the log field 'service' in app-254-prod-logs over the same window are Company.Ops (7 documents) and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (5 documents); the level distribution is ERROR 5, INFO 5 and WARN 2, and correlation_ids are dr-test-001 (5), radar-cycle-445 (2), radar-cycle-446 (2), job-8827 (1), job-8831 (1) and radar-cycle-447 (1).
Service Company.Ops logged at 2026-11-23T11:12:49Z on host ops-prod-01: INFO 'DR test initiated - switching to failover database' with correlation_id dr-test-001 and environment production.

Service Company.Ops logged ERRORs at 2026-11-23T12:12:49Z: 'Job scheduler failed to process batch: connection timeout to failover DB after 30s' (correlation_id dr-test-001) and 'Scheduled job execution failed with status 500: unable to acquire database lock during failover' (correlation_id job-8827), both on host ops-prod-01.
Service Company.Ops logged at 2026-11-23T13:12:49Z on host ops-prod-02: WARN 'Job creation endpoint returning 503 - database failover in progress' with correlation_id dr-test-001.

The new-scheduled-job failure appears in the index as service Company.Ops, host ops-prod-02, 2026-11-23T14:12:49Z, correlation_id job-8831, level ERROR: 'Failed to create new scheduled job: HTTP 500 - transaction deadlock detected on jobs table'; this is the only returned document describing creation of a new scheduled job.

Service Company.Ops logged INFO at 2026-11-23T15:12:49Z on ops-prod-01 'DR test failover completed - primary database restored' (dr-test-001) and at 2026-11-23T16:12:49Z on ops-prod-01 'Job scheduler resumed normal operation'; no ERROR-level document later than 2026-11-23T14:12:49Z was returned in this window.

Service Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (a different entity from companyopswebjob) logged its own failures during the same failover: ERROR at 2026-11-23T12:12:49Z 'Radar batch processing failed: upstream dependency Company.Ops unavailable during failover' (radar-cycle-445, host radar-prod-01), ERROR at 2026-11-23T13:12:49Z 'Job execution error: HTTP 500 from internal API - database connection pool exhausted' (radar-cycle-446), WARN at 2026-11-23T14:12:49Z 'Retrying failed radar collection job after backoff', then INFO at 2026-11-23T15:12:49Z 'Radar data collection resumed successfully after failover recovery' (radar-cycle-447).

A full-text search of app-254-prod-logs for the exact string 'companyopswebjob' across the authorized window returned 0 documents, and the aggregation of all 12 documents in 10:00:00Z–17:12:59Z shows no service value other than Company.Ops and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob.

The 500/503 errors recorded by Company.Ops (batch processing timeout to failover DB, database lock acquisition failure during failover, job-creation 500 with transaction deadlock on the jobs table) were caused by the planned DR failover of its database that it logged as initiated at 11:12:49Z: every error message names the failover as the condition, the errors start one hour after the failover began, and they stop after 'DR test failover completed - primary database restored' at 15:12:49Z. The failover database itself is not a named or observable object in the evidence, so this remains a hypothesis.

An alternative candidate not excluded by the logs is an application-level concurrency defect independent of the failover: 'transaction deadlock detected on jobs table' (job-8831, 14:12:49Z) and 'database connection pool exhausted' (radar-cycle-446, 13:12:49Z) describe internal database contention that the log text does not prove was introduced by the failover; no deadlock counter, lock-wait metric or query plan evidence was available to decide between them.

The user's 'companyopswebjob' most plausibly refers to the entity logged as Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob, which is the only webjob-like service in this index and which logged 500s and a dependency failure during the same window; this is name-similarity only and is not established, since no service named companyopswebjob appears anywhere in the 12 documents.

The impact was not open at the end of the observed log set: Company.Ops logged 'DR test failover completed - primary database restored' at 15:12:49Z and 'Job scheduler resumed normal operation' at 16:12:49Z, and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob logged 'Radar data collection resumed successfully after failover recovery' at 15:12:49Z, so the returned logs show recovery within the window, not continued failure.

gaps: No log document in app-254-prod-logs carries the service name companyopswebjob (a full-text search for that string returned nothing, which shows only that this query matched nothing); whether such a service logs elsewhere is unknown.
Jaeger trace listing returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no spans, per-operation error status or latency for Company.Ops or Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob could be examined.
Prometheus label queries on traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no service inventory, error-rate or latency series could corroborate or date the 500s.

The Kubernetes cluster reachable here is the otel-demo demo cluster: a deployment query over all namespaces for names matching ops|radar|webjob returned no objects out of 24 deployments, so I could not inspect pod status, restart reasons, events or container logs for Company.Ops or Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob in the production environment.

The failover database and the DR test harness are not named objects in any evidence (no host, cluster, service or config object), so the mechanism by which the failover produced connection timeouts and a jobs-table deadlock cannot be verified.

Log timestamps are writer-supplied and the 12 documents are spaced at exactly one hour (11:12:49Z–16:12:49Z), which is consistent with sampled or synthetic emission; the true error rate and the precise onset/end of failures between those samples are unknown.
No user-request identifier, HTTP access log or request latency record for the specific new-scheduled-job attempt is present, so the single job-8831 line is the only trace of that user action.
next_steps: Ask the user to confirm the exact production service name (Company.Ops vs Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob vs a separate companyopswebjob deployment) and its log index, so the exact entity can be queried.

Obtain the DR test runbook/change record for correlation_id dr-test-001 (failover start 2026-11-23T11:12:49Z, completion 15:12:49Z) to confirm the failover database identity and whether the observed timeout/deadlock errors are known effects.

Provide Jaeger and Prometheus connectivity (or per-service error/latency dashboards) for the production cluster to check whether the 500s were confined to job creation or affected all Company.Ops operations, and to compare against a pre-failover baseline.

If the production cluster is accessible, pull Company.Ops and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob pod events, container restart reasons and application logs for 2026-11-23T11:00Z–16:30Z, plus any networkpolicy/endpoint/resourcequota state, to test the failover hypothesis against an application-level lock/connection-pool defect.
For the jobs-table deadlock specifically, ask the database team for lock-wait/deadlock metrics and slow-query logs for the jobs table during 12:00Z–15:00Z.
